analysis.title: GS Overlay - Issue 036 Oil Expression: The $27 Risk Premium
key_insights: Brent has risen to roughly $112/bbl on escalating Middle East tensions and growing downside risks to supply, which have increased precautionary buying in physical and financial markets.

GS estimates Brent fair value at approximately $85/bbl, implying a geopolitical risk premium of roughly $27/bbl. Daan Struyven assesses that essentially all of the recent rise in crude reflects a higher risk premium, not a higher fair value.

The underlying oil balance has changed less than the price. Market-price risks are now increasingly symmetric, and the path depends on whether supply risks intensify or a durable diplomatic resolution lets the premium unwind.
Preferred expression: hedge geopolitical oil-price upside selectively.
Brent is steeply backwardated. The forward curve falls from roughly $114/bbl at the front to the high-$80s by late 2027, which points to substantial normalization from current levels.

Brent has stayed elevated while the Geopolitical Risk Index retraced from recent spikes. The risk premium is not only a function of headline risk: precautionary physical buying, supply-chain disruption and financial hedging demand also support prices.

Brent and the US 2Y Treasury yield have both risen materially over the past year and moved sharply higher again through September and October, linking higher energy costs to tighter financial conditions.
